text:
alex: FYI ran into a weird interaction between structlog, our OTEL middleware, and the async Python client — request_id sometimes drifts between concurrent requests when using the shared AsyncClient.
maria: ugh that sounds bad. is the SDK setting headers globally or using contextvars? can you paste a repro?
alex: minimal repro below — spawn two tasks that call the client concurrently, one sets X-Request-ID in the logger via a contextvar. sometimes the second request logs the first request's id.
alex: ```python
import asyncio
import contextvars
from httpx import AsyncClient

request_id = contextvars.ContextVar('request_id', default=None)

async def call(idx):
    request_id.set(f'req-{idx}')
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        # sdk wraps httpx and injects headers from tracing middleware
        await c.get('https://example.local/data')

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(call(1), call(2))

asyncio.run(main())
```
alex: sometimes logs show req-1 for both calls.
maria: do we know if Redwood py-sdk uses a global session or reuses headers object across tasks? that smells like shared mutable state in the middleware.
derek: I think our middleware mutates a dict on the client instance when adding trace headers; in sync path we copy but in async path we forgot to copy for performance reasons. copying should be cheap and safe.
jean: another angle: structlog integration expects request_id via contextvar when formatting. If our middleware doesn't run in the same context (asyncio.create_task breaks context depending on how it's used) that can cause mismatch.
alex: exactly — the symptoms only happen under heavy concurrency (fast tasks), and when using our SDK's OTEL auto-instrumentor + structlog processors.
maria: small repro suggestion: try forcing context propagation by using asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task vs directly creating tasks — but we should fix SDK instead of workarounds.
derek: agreed. patch idea: ensure middleware uses immutable header mapping per request and avoid mutating client-level state. Also ensure we restore or capture current contextvars when scheduling background work. I'll draft a PR.
jean: typing/SDK DX note — middleware hooks are currently untyped (Any params) which makes it easy to accidentally mutate structures. We should add a Protocol/TypedHook signature in the public py-sdk types so middleware authors get IDE help.
alex: +1 on typed hooks. Also request: can we expose a small example app that shows correct structlog + otel + py-sdk setup? that would save onboarding friction.
maria: good call — sample app could live under examples/observability/ with tests that assert request_id is preserved under concurrency.
derek: I'll open two GH issues: 1) bug: async middleware mutating headers (assign to me). 2) enhancement: typed middleware hook + example app (assign to jean).
ci-bot: created issues #4123 and #4124 and linked PR template.
alex: thanks! one more runtime note: if we change default behavior to copy headers per-request it may slightly increase allocations. we should add a microbenchmark and document the perf tradeoff in the PR.
jean: will do. also I'll propose adding a small helper util in the SDK to attach request_id from contextvar to structlog processors and to the OTEL span attributes, so apps don't have to wire both.
alex: perfect. action items summary: Derek -> bug fix PR (async header immutability), Jean -> typed hook + example app + structlog helper, Maria -> add unit + concurrency tests, Alex -> add microbench and verify sample app. I'll follow up in the GH issues with repro artifacts. :thumbsup:
